fixes.explanation: Not a treaty, friend. The envoy says, “Rise up, and let us go to battle against her!” (Obadiah 1:1). That's a call to battle, and the “her” is Edom. I think Edom would have preferred the paperwork.

True! The LORD says, “Though you soar like the eagle and make your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down…” (Obadiah 1:4). A nest among the stars doesn't change anything. The LORD says that even from there He will bring Edom down.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “But how Esau will be pillaged, his hidden treasures sought out!” (Obadiah 1:6). Thieves would steal only what they wanted, but this is different. Esau's hidden treasures get sought out.

That's the opposite of what the LORD says. Thieves might take only what they wanted, but for Esau the LORD says, “But how Esau will be pillaged, his hidden treasures sought out!” (Obadiah 1:6). Hidden treasures are exactly what gets sought out.
Nobody is handing anything out. The LORD says Esau will be pillaged and his hidden treasures sought out (Obadiah 1:6). That's taking, not giving.
That's the one. “Those who eat your bread will set a trap for you without your awareness of it.” (Obadiah 1:7). The trap comes without Edom's awareness of it. I think that's the part that stings.

I see why you'd pick it, since we're talking about eating bread. But the verse says those who eat Edom's bread “…will set a trap for you…” (Obadiah 1:7). A feast doesn't fit, because the verse names a trap. Bread is in the verse, but a party isn't.
You got it. The LORD says, “Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified…” (Obadiah 1:9). Terrified is the word for the mighty men of Teman. I'm just glad nobody asked me to be a mighty man.

Mighty men do sound like they'd stand firm, I'll give you that. But the LORD says, “Then your mighty men, O Teman, will be terrified…” (Obadiah 1:9). Terrified is the word the LORD uses, and standing firm isn't in the verse.

No victory is mentioned for them in this verse. The LORD says the mighty men of Teman “…will be terrified…” (Obadiah 1:9). Terrified is what the verse says about them. This is a heavy part of the vision.

That's the reason, baker. The LORD says, “Because of the violence against your brother Jacob, you will be covered with shame and cut off forever.” (Obadiah 1:10). The LORD calls Jacob Edom's brother. This is a heavy verse.

Not quite. Verse 11 does say Edom stood aloof while strangers carried off Jacob's wealth. But the reason in verse 10 is “Because of the violence against your brother Jacob…” (Obadiah 1:10). The verse names violence against Jacob, not refusing to fight the nations.

True. The LORD says, “Nor should you stand at the crossroads to cut off their fugitives…” (Obadiah 1:14). The fugitives are from the people of Judah, and the crossroads is where Edom should not be standing. The verse goes on to say Edom should not deliver up their survivors.

It's true. The LORD says, “Nor should you stand at the crossroads to cut off their fugitives, nor deliver up their survivors in the day of their distress.” (Obadiah 1:14). Standing at the crossroads to cut off fugitives is on the list of things the LORD says Edom should not do.
